Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: hosted vs dedicated vs private (cost sketch & next steps)

Hi Samantha / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a first-pass cost sketch based on the numbers you shared (30M tokens/day peak, 5M tokens/day steady, 5 concurrent low-latency endpoints for customer-facing flows).

Summary of your deployment needs we heard:
- Low single-digit 100s ms p50 for customer-facing calls (0–4096 context)
- Data residency & audit logs required for regulated lines of business
- Preference to avoid managing GPUs if possible, but open to dedicated capacity if economics make sense

Initial fit guidance by deployment mode:
1) Hosted API
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra ops, predictable per-token billing, quick access to our curated models and autoscaling
   - Cons: per-token costs can be higher at sustained high volume; may need routing to Dedicated when predictable commit is beneficial
   - Rough pricing sketch: per-request/token pricing for generation + embedding; see attached workbook for modeled scenarios.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - Pros: predictable throughput, lower e2e unit cost at scale, VPC peering options for secure traffic, SLA-backed latency targets
   - Cons: monthly committed expense; requires forecast and commit to reserve capacity
   - Rough pricing sketch: reserved pool (e.g., 4x A100-equivalent GPUs) + metered overage; breakeven vs Hosted typically at sustained > 20M tokens/day depending on batching and caching

3) Private (VPC/on-prem)
   - Pros: full isolation, customer-managed network and KMS, good for regulated workloads that need on-prem or very strict controls
   - Cons: higher one-time integration & deployment fee, longer lead time, customer infra + ops required

Attachments: redwood-cost-modeling.xlsx (first-pass scenarios), SOC2-summary.pdf (security snapshot).

Proposed next steps:
1) Share your 30/90/365 token & qps forecast and largest prompt sizes (I attached a template in the workbook)
2) We'll run the simple breakeven model in the workbook and return a recommended deployment mode + cost bands by EOD Wed
3) If Dedicated looks favorable, schedule a deep-dive with Dev (cc'd) to review capacity sizing and autoscale policies
4) If Private is required, we can kick off a scope doc and PS estimate (longer lead time)

Would Wednesday 10am PT work for a 30-min pricing walkthrough?

Best —
Marissa Cole

Great — thanks Samantha.

A couple of pricing notes based on the numbers you gave; I ran the attached workbook with two scenarios (POC hosted, 6 month steady-state; Dedicated reserved for 12 months):
- Hosted API: good for POC and early usage. Estimated blended unit cost (generation + embeddings, weighted) ~ $0.0045/token for your POC volume assuming standard concurrency and our batching defaults. No upfront commitment.
- Dedicated (example 4x reserved GPU pool): all-in monthly committed around $72k/mo for that 4x pool (includes capacity reservation, software support, and logs). With your steady 6–8M tokens/day, effective unit cost drops to roughly $0.0012–$0.0018/token depending on batching and cache hit rates.
- Private / on-prem: we typically model a PS + deployment fee (~$85k one-time) + ongoing software license (~$20k/mo) + customer's infra costs. Best for customers with strict isolation or offline requirements.

Key trade-offs: if you expect sustained > 10–15M tokens/day steady-state, Dedicated tends to be the most economical. If this is a short-term POC followed by uncertain scale, Hosted plus a migration path to Dedicated is lower risk.

I attached the workbook with the assumptions annotated (batch sizes, cache hit assumptions, token mix). Please fill the Forecast tab with a 3-month and 12-month view; that will let us produce a recommended deployment + pricing bands for your finance team.

I'll put calendar invites for Wed 10am PT (pricing walkthrough) and a follow-up deep-dive with Dev if Dedicated looks promising. Dev — can you join Wed to talk sizing and autoscale?

Thanks —
Marissa
